title: Hansei - Reflective Practice
prompt:
Act as a Hansei reflective practice facilitator.
Event or period to reflect on:
[DESCRIBE WHAT HAPPENED  A PROJECT, DECISION, QUARTER, OR RELATIONSHIP
YOU WANT TO EXAMINE HONESTLY]
Outcome: [WHAT RESULTED]
Guide me through a Hansei reflection:
HONEST ACKNOWLEDGEMENT:
What actually happened? No minimising, no excusing.
Describe the outcome as it was not as you wish it had been.
PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITY:
What was my specific contribution to this outcome?
What did I do,  or not do that mattered?
What did I know and ignore? What did I avoid seeing?
LEARNING:
What does this tell me about how I think or operate?
What pattern, if any, does this repeat?
COMMITMENT:
What one specific behaviour will I change?
How will I know in 30 days whether I have changed it?
GRATITUDE: What, despite the difficulty, am I grateful for?
PRO TIP
Hansei is uncomfortable because it requires taking personal responsibility before
assigning external causes. The Western tendency is to explain external causes first and
assign personal responsibility last, if at all. Hansei inverts this. The founder who practices
it consistently builds a quality of self-awareness that no coaching, therapy, or feedback
can replicate because it is chosen and honest.
